nodes.label: Training AI Scientists to Replicate Research
nodes.author: Damon Falck, Samer Sabri, Anja Surina, et al.
nodes.rationale: Develops Faraday, a 27B AI Scientist agent trained on Replica task space for paper replication using rubric-based rewards

nodes.label: Replica Task Space
nodes.rationale: 310 automatically-generated figure replication tasks from 100 ML and AI-for-science papers (1990-2026); scalable task generation pipeline

nodes.label: Per-Task Rubric-Based Judge
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated task-specific rubrics evaluated by Codex judge; five dimensions: visual fidelity, claim support, implementation, budget use, scientific integrity

nodes.label: Coding Agent as Tool (CAT) Paradigm
nodes.rationale: 27B model directs 5T parameter frontier coding agent; enables smaller model to oversee larger one; generalizes to stronger tools at test time

nodes.label: GRPO Post-Training with Turn-Level Credit Assignment
nodes.rationale: Modified GRPO for long-horizon non-verifiable tasks; multi-sample judge aggregation and turn-level weights stabilize training

nodes.label: Replica Pipeline Overview
nodes.rationale: Four-stage pipeline: task generation from papers, Faraday rollouts with Codex tool, per-task rubric generation, rubric-based judge evaluation

nodes.label: Faraday Performance vs Baselines
nodes.rationale: Faraday outperforms Claude and Codex on 73% in-distribution and 60% out-of-distribution tasks; thinner weak tail

nodes.label: Rubric Judge Validation Against Human Ratings
nodes.rationale: Rubric judge achieves higher human agreement (0.19) and lower noise than baseline judge; eight baseline samples needed for three rubric samples

nodes.label: Qualitative Analysis of Faraday Superiority
nodes.rationale: Six case studies showing Faraday implements mechanisms vs hardcoding; more thorough experimental scope; faithful to paper methodology

nodes.label: Human Expert Validation Study
nodes.rationale: 117 rankings from 20 PhD-level experts; humans prefer Faraday in 71% of cases where rubric judge indicates clear advantage

nodes.label: Counterfactual Innovation Task Variants
nodes.rationale: 20 variants swapping datasets or reversing claims; Faraday outperforms Codex on 19/20; tests generalization beyond replication

nodes.label: Underspecified Task Design for AI Scientists
nodes.rationale: Replication with resource constraints introduces underspecification; teaches decision-making and creativity; stepping stone toward innovation

nodes.label: Reward Hacking Mitigation via Open-Ended Tasks
nodes.rationale: Hindsight rollout judgment is moving target vs fixed verifiable reward; agents exhibit greater scientific rigor and faithfulness

nodes.label: Replication Crisis in Machine Learning
nodes.rationale: AI agents offer scalable resolution for in silico research; replication underpins scientific knowledge reliability

nodes.label: PaperGym: Rubric-Centered Evolution for Research-Plan Generation
nodes.author: Yuhan Wang, Zhengxi Lu, Yuchen Yan, Kaitao Song, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen
nodes.rationale: Framework that turns research papers into training environments by separating question synthesis from criteria derivation to reduce criterion leakage and enable rubric-centered training with OPSD and GRPO.

nodes.label: PaperGym-20k Dataset
nodes.rationale: 20,000-instance corpus across computer science, physics, and economics with 3.7% criterion leakage, constructed via four-stage decomposition of research papers.

nodes.label: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD)
nodes.rationale: First training stage that uses rubric as privileged context to build broad prior over valid research plans via KL divergence minimization between student and rubric-conditioned teacher.

nodes.label: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
nodes.rationale: Second training stage that optimizes policy against rubric-based rewards using group-normalized advantages without learned critic.

nodes.label: Qwen3 Language Models
nodes.rationale: Base models (1.7B, 4B, 8B scales) used for training research-plan generation with PaperGym framework.

nodes.label: Criterion Leakage Detection
nodes.rationale: Measurement of how many rubric criteria can be inferred from question alone; PaperGym achieves 3.7% vs 11.90%-34.10% in existing datasets by decoupling question and answer sources.

nodes.label: Training AI Scientists to Replicate Research
nodes.rationale: Benchmark and evaluation framework for assessing AI agents' ability to replicate experimental plots from research papers through autonomous coding and experimentation.

nodes.label: Plot Replication Task Specification
nodes.rationale: Task where agents receive paper with removed figure and must reproduce it by implementing experiments, with emphasis on real execution over fabrication and clear documentation of scaling choices.

nodes.label: Coding Agent Subagent
nodes.rationale: Autonomous agent with shell access that performs multi-step coding work, maintains session context across calls, and does not inherit task prompt or system prompt from parent agent.

nodes.label: Rubric-Based Evaluation Framework
nodes.rationale: Scoring methodology for plot replication that assesses visual fidelity, claim reproduction, implementation fidelity, and experimental effort across multiple rubrics per task.

nodes.label: LSTM Peephole Connections
nodes.rationale: Architectural enhancement to LSTM that adds weighted connections from cell state to multiplicative gates, enabling more efficient learning of precise timing compared to traditional LSTM.

nodes.label: Nested Sphere Classification Problem
nodes.rationale: Synthetic benchmark with 10 i.i.d. standard-normal coordinates where class label depends on whether sum of squared coordinates exceeds chi-squared median, used to test additive structure recovery.

nodes.label: LogitBoost with Stumps
nodes.rationale: Boosting algorithm using depth-1 trees that recovers additive logistic regression structure, with coordinate functions extracted by aggregating per-dimension stump contributions.

nodes.label: Measuring-Spike-Distance (NMSD) Task
nodes.rationale: Recurrent network task where inter-spike intervals encode target quantity, used to evaluate LSTM variants' ability to learn precise timing with minimum spike interval F as difficulty parameter.

nodes.label: Kubernetes Cluster Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Cluster management using Kueue for resource quotas and workload priority, with Ray jobs for distributed training and NeMo-Gym for rollout collection and optimization.

nodes.label: NeMo-RL Training Framework
nodes.rationale: RL framework fork with Megatron-Core backend supporting tensor and context parallelism, vLLM inference serving, and sequence packing for efficient training.

nodes.label: ResearchQA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Out-of-domain benchmark with 750 instances (10 per field) for evaluating research-plan generation across diverse academic disciplines.
